Mokobody Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mokobody, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Mokobody from the 18th century, peaking at 486 residents in 1884 before emigration and WWI reduced the population to 290 by 1921; most were murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery's exact founding is unknown but confirmed by 1845-1847 burial-fee records. Poland closed the cemetery in 1963, describing it as abandoned since 1944. A 1989 inspection found human bones surfacing due to locals stealing sand from the grounds - a sports field had since occupied part of the site - prompting the Commune head to rebury the bones, scatter tombstone fragments to deter further theft, and install a plaque reading: 'The Jewish cemetery in Mokobody. Closed for burial purposes, legally protected.'
